text:
The Ducks are 11-9-1 and 6-3-1 in their last ten, and the reason is easy to name: Cutter Gauthier has scored in nine straight games. He has 19 points in his last ten, Beckett Sennecke has 17, and the two of them with Mikael Granlund have outscored opponents 7-4 together. Sunday's 6-1 rout of Calgary was the full version of what this team can look like when everything goes in.

The worry is what's underneath. Anaheim has taken 49.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and just 47% at five on five, and it has scored 8.6 more goals than its chances deserve. Even that top line gives up more than it creates. On the back end, Jackson LaCombe's two most-used pairings have been outchanced badly, around 36 to 37% of the expected goals. And Lukas Dostal is in a rut, .832 with 4.5 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, while Laurent Brossoit has been the steadier hand lately.

Our simulations give the Ducks a 64% shot at the playoffs, a projected 91 points. That's a real team with a real chance. Whether it holds depends on the chances catching up with the finishing before the finishing cools, and on which goalie claims the net.
